<!-- pr-reviewer: 5e4f83400aadc69290afa4a913f99839f2b81d29 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- G17 rides the engage/cancel G01 block (`G17 G01 G42 ...`), selected before the comp word, which is valid on Fanuc/Haas/Mazak and 840D (a plane word in the same block ahead of G41/G42; the plane is not changed while comp is already active). `compPlaneWord` is applied at fanuc.cps:408 and the equivalent lines in haas/mazak/sinumerik.
- The cancel case is covered: once an XZ/YZ arc under comp is refused, comp is only ever engaged in G17, so G40 always executes in G17; and the G40 block itself carries G17 when needed (it goes through the same `compPlaneWord(cg)`).
- Other plane-change paths checked: canned cycles call `restorePlane()` (a cycle inside comp is already refused by `onRadiusCompensation`/`compRefuse`); an arc arriving between the COMP record and the engage block hits `compRefuse` (warning); comp left on at section end warns (fanuc.cps:370) after `restorePlane()`; helical arcs in G17 are unaffected; XZ/YZ helicals under comp are refused by `compPlaneRefuse`. I found no gap.
- Refusal is a counted warning via `msg()`, nothing written for the arc; it is in the script, so it applies on every post path.
- Clean-room: no external material; comments cite RS-274/ISO 6983. Decision doc present, body ends `Fixes #391`, has `Changelog:`. No goldens changed.

**Local results (merged with current origin/main, clean merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-post, all binaries (axis_direction_cli 3, comp 9, comp_plane 3, post_engine 33) | pass |
| app control_comp 5, wear_comp 5, conformance 6, golden_cl 23, fanuc_post 8, posting 17, inverted_post 15, inverted_equivalence 2 | pass |
| clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |
| Revert check: fanuc.cps with the two helpers' call sites removed | `every_comp_post_states_g17...` and `...refuses_an_xz_or_yz_arc...` FAIL as claimed; the G17-only test still passes |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The pinning test only exercises the Rapid/Plunge/Feed record shapes, not a cycle-with-comp stream; that path is already refused elsewhere, so fine.
- The test reads `G` words left to right, which matches the plane-before-comp ordering these posts write; worth keeping if the block order ever changes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
